question: What are the design features and operational parameters of high-temperature and low-temperature plasma reactors used for reactive nitrogen species production?
answer: High-temperature plasma reactors utilize double concentric glass/quartz tubes for heat exchange and dielectric barrier discharge, with an AC high voltage of 13.6 kVp-p at 12.5 kHz applied between a central SUS wire and a grounded SUS pipe. These reactors have a discharge coupling power of approximately 44 W, leading to an adiabatic temperature rise of about 2000 K, which selectively produces nitric oxide and nitrogen dioxide. Low-temperature plasma reactors employ typical dielectric barrier discharge geometry powered by a voltage- and frequency-variable AC supply, operating at 7.8 kVp-p and 5.7 kHz with a discharge coupling power of 3.4 W. These reactors primarily produce ozone while minimizing nitrogen dissociation, ensuring stable species composition and operational durability for continuous use over extended periods.

The paper aims to develop a novel synthesis method for dinitrogen pentoxide (N2O5) using air and electricity via discharge plasmas, eliminating the need for hazardous raw materials. The authors demonstrate the nitrating capability of the N2O5-rich plasma effluent gas on tyrosine, highlighting its potential for widespread scientific and industrial applications.
